import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Symptom

The operator boots (HTTP `/api/health` responds, MCP works) but the **entire DBOS
background system is silently dead**: no `routinesTick`, so **git-sync stops
committing**, **green-checkpoint / release-trigger stop** (deploys freeze, `main`
goes stale), scheduled-plan fires stop, and `fleet:place_batch` 500s. The boot log
has the tell:

```
[endpoint-ipc] failed to start: .../harness/routines/schedule-next.ts:14
import { RRule, RRuleSet } from 'rrule';
SyntaxError: The requested module 'rrule' does not provide an export named 'RRule'
[dbos] boot failed (non-fatal): The requested module 'rrule' does not provide an export named 'RRule'
```

`[dbos] boot failed (non-fatal)` is the line that matters — "non-fatal" means the
HTTP host stays up, so health/MCP look fine while every routine-driven subsystem is
down. On 2026-06-17 this took prod (`:3070`) down for ~2h and stranded ~650 files of
fleet work uncommitted (git-sync is itself a routine, so it died too).

## Root cause

`rrule` is a **CommonJS** package. Under the operator's ESM/tsx host, a CJS module's
classes are exposed on the **default export**, not as statically-detectable named
exports — so `import { RRule, RRuleSet } from 'rrule'` throws `does not provide an
export named 'RRule'` **at module load**. Any module that statically imports the
offender (here `claim.ts → schedule-next.ts`) fails to load, and because
`routinesTick`'s import graph reaches it, the whole tick fails to register.

<Aside type="danger" title="vitest does NOT catch this">
The named import passes the unit + integration suites (vitest's CJS interop resolves
the named export) and the SPA build (Vite handles CJS). It only throws under **tsx**,
which is what the operator runs. So a green test run + green deploy can still ship a
DBOS-killing regression. Verify a backend `rrule` (or any CJS-only dep) consumer with
a real tsx import, not just vitest.
</Aside>

## Fix — load CJS deps via createRequire

```ts
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
// rrule is CJS: its classes are on the default export, NOT statically-detectable
// named exports under ESM/tsx. createRequire resolves them at runtime.
const { RRule, RRuleSet } = createRequire(import.meta.url)('rrule') as typeof import('rrule');
```

This is the repo's ESM-safe CJS pattern (cf. `libs/generic/resource-profile`). The
`as typeof import('rrule')` keeps the static types. **Frontend** code (operator-vite)
can keep the named import — Vite bundles CJS fine; this is a **backend/tsx-only** trap.

## Verify before you ship a backend CJS consumer

```bash
npx tsx -e "import('./packages/operator-core/lib/.../your-module.ts').then(m => console.log('loaded', !!m))"
```

If it prints `loaded`, the module loads under the runtime the operator uses. A passing
`vitest run` alone does not prove this.

## Recovery, if it already shipped

The deadlock: git-sync (dead) can't commit the fix; the routine tick (dead) can't
deploy it. Break it manually — minimal one-file commit of the fix + push `staging`,
then the **sanctioned incident path** `tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts
--deploy-commit <sha> --execute` (needs `PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1` to permit the
restart). Once `:3070` reboots on the fix, DBOS relaunches and git-sync sweeps the
backlog normally.

See also [Scheduled plans](/internal/docs/spec/scheduled-plans) (the routine this
import feeds) and the design [libraries](/internal/docs/design/libraries) note.
